en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the injustices of Spanish colonial rule in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the Philippines and serves as the final interpreter of the Philippine Constitution.
The Ifugao people of the Cordillera region built the Banaue Rice Terraces, which are carved into the mountains and recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a makeshift incubator using bamboo baskets.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo, Aklan, honors the Santo Niño and features participants painting their faces with black soot to mimic the Ati people.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its pristine coral reefs and marine biodiversity.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, from the balcony of his home in Kawit, Cavite.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system that uses characters to represent syllables and is still used in modern cultural designs today.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884 for his famous masterpiece Spoliarium.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right and duty to vote in national elections.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan is visually represented by neighbors helping a family move their entire nipa hut to a new location.
